title: Chaptered Lit Cribs: Context Efficiency & KV Cache Reads
content:
Quick framing:
- Trying to capture a lightweight, chaptered digest of papers/blogs that matter for context efficiency and KV cache patterns. Not a polished lit review — more like crib notes I can paste into Slack or a PR.

Top-level takeaways (high-level brain dump):
- Small wins multiply: prefix caching + inexpensive eviction heuristics can cut token compute by 20-60% depending on workload.
- Workload shape matters: highly-repetitive assistant sessions benefit most from prefix/KV reuse; long unique documents benefit more from chunked retrieval than KV cache.
- Eviction policy is a knob we under-explore: recency + semantic salience hybrid seems promising; LRU alone often tosses useful long-range items.
- Quantization interacts with cache effectiveness — lower precision kernels change memory/throughput balance and can make KV caching more attractive on mid-range GPUs.

Papers & posts I flagged (very short notes):
- "KV Cache at Scale" (blog, 2025) — practical heuristics for shard placement, async eviction, and partial KV fetch for streaming. Implementation-first; good for ops-level bullet points.
- "Prefix Caching & Prefix Merging" (paper, NeurIPS 2024) — formalizes when prefixes can be merged; has bounds on correctness when merging similar prefixes. Good section on merge error.
- "Sparse Retrieval Meets KV" (ICLR 2026) — hybrid approach: retrieve dense context, then store compressed KV fingerprints for cheap rehydrate. Inspires "fingerprint bloom" idea below.
- "Quantization Effects on Attention State" (workshop paper, 2026) — small experiments showing that 8-bit attention kernels preserve logits well but amplify KV storage noise; suggests heavier compression only on keys, not values.
- "Latency-First Batching" (engineering blog) — continuous batching tweaks that minimize p99 regression for interactive workloads; useful for Dedicated capacity config notes.

Notes / excerpts I want to remember: (half-formed)
- "prefix merge": only safe if shared subsequence probability > threshold; need to measure false-positive merge rate on our chat logs.
- Async eviction: evict in background to avoid p99 spikes on serving path. But watch for eviction lag causing memory pressure.
- Fingerprint store: store compact (e.g., 256-bit) LSH of context windows to detect re-occurrence cheaply; on match, schedule full KV retrieval from slower tier.

Experiment shortlist (quick, prioritize cheap infra first):
1) Measure real-world prefix reuse on hosted API logs (last 30d): compute fraction of tokens that could be reused by exact prefix match vs fuzzy match (edit-distance / embedding sim). Metric: token_reuse_pct, p50/p95 latency diff when cache hit vs miss. (JIRA-ENG-4127).
2) Small on-prem bench: deploy hybrid store (hot KV in-GPU, warm in-CPU DRAM) with background prefetch for predicted next-window; compare cost per token vs baseline for simulated chat traces (10k sessions).
3) Eviction ablation: LRU vs recency+salience (salience = sum token TF-IDF over doc) vs learned (small MLP predicting next-access). Measure hit-rate vs cache size.
4) Quantization impact: bench 16-bit vs 8-bit kernels with identical cache sizes; note degradation patterns and whether compressing keys only helps.

Immediate actionables (my TODOs):
- [ ] Script to extract prefix reuse histogram from hosted logs (approx: sample 1M requests, build prefix trie). Target Feb-ish? (actually: do this now; blocking: log retention access).
- [ ] Prototype tiny fingerprint bloomstore (Python + Faiss L2 hashing) and run on 100k windows from reddit+internal-sample; estimate false-positive rate.
- [ ] Slack a question to #serving-runtime: "do we currently track cumulative token reuse percent per user-session?" (tag: @Samir).

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Cost model: when does the overhead of maintaining KV (memory + eviction) exceed the token savings? Need a simple cost calculator that includes GPU memory opportunity cost.
- How often do our customers have long tail contexts that are semantically similar but not lexically? Embedding-sim reuse might be useful but expensive.
- Is there an easy, low-risk rollout path (canary) for prefix caching that won’t cause quality regressions? Need eval harness that scores generation difference on a set of prompts.

Handy links I keep referencing (to paste into PRs):
- Internal playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/KV+Cache+Playbook
- GH experiment repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments
- Notebook with reuse histograms (early): GH#notebooks/prefix-reuse-exploration.ipynb

Mini shorthand glossary (for my future self):
- KV: key-value cache (attention key/values per layer)
- Prefix merge: combining two similar prefixes in cache to avoid duplication
- Fingerprint bloom: tiny LSH/fingerprint to cheaply detect likely repeats
- Hot/warm tiers: hot = GPU-resident, warm = host RAM or SSD-backed compressed store

One-paragraph note I can paste in a PR description:
"This doc collects quick findings and immediate experiments for reducing token compute via prefix/KV caching. Short-term experiments focus on measuring real prefix reuse in production traces, prototyping a compact fingerprint layer to cheaply detect repeats, and running eviction-policy ablations. The goal is to build a low-risk canary that proves meaningful token reductions without degrading generation quality — ideally a 20–40% reduction on chat-heavy workloads."

Random personal notes / scratch (do not ship):
- If we can compress keys with asymmetric quantization (keys low-bit, values higher-bit) we might cut hot memory in half with small quality hit. Worth exploring on small stable weights models first.
- Think about UI in Console: show token_savings_estimate per-route from caching heuristics. Simple % and expected $ saved/month. Good sales fodder.

End of crib. Will iterate after the prefix-hist script lands.
